verdicts.argument: The comparator of `body.sort` is mutated, and V8's Array.prototype.sort (TimSort: binary insertion, run detection, galloping) only ever asks whether the comparator's result is NEGATIVE. Pristine returns a negative value exactly when a < b. Under this mutant the comparator still returns a negative value exactly when a < b or a === b (for `a <= b` in the first position: an equal pair now compares negative; equal lines are byte-identical strings, so whichever is placed first the joined output is the same bytes; for `a <= b` in the second position: a > b returns 0 and a === b returns 1, both non-negative), so every decision the sort takes is the same and the sorted array is the same. Supplementary direct check (not the verdict): 3,000 pseudo-random arrays of up to 2,500 strings, with and without many duplicates, sorted under node v24.22.1 by the pristine comparator and by each of the five comparator mutants of this line: 0 of 15,000 results differ. The battery was re-run for this mutant with p20 (300 cases in a fixed pseudo-random order, enough to reach the merge and gallop paths) added to both missions: still IDENTICAL on every leg.

The state reaching the post-loop checks (stack, seenRoot, body) is the one the pristine loop exits with. p18 (no final newline) is the document that reaches that offset.

verdicts.argument: This is the `stack.length === 0` operand of the end-tag guard `!m || stack.length === 0 || stack[stack.length - 1] !== m[1]`. With it forced false, an end tag met while the stack is empty is still refused by the third operand: `stack[stack.length - 1]` is `stack[-1]`, which is undefined, and `m[1]` is a non-empty name matched by `[A-Za-z_][\w.:-]*`, so `undefined !== m[1]` is true and the function returns null exactly as before. When the stack is not empty the operand was false anyway. Measured on f17 (a stray `</x>` after the root) and f18 (a stray `</x>` before the root), the two documents that reach it: both still unprojected, sealed by bytes.
